extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants (KIPO / Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Examination guidelines from the Korean Intellectual Property Office covering deposit rules for microorganisms, sequence listing requirements, and core patentability standards (industrial applicability, statutory invention, novelty, utility model distinctions). Intended to guide formalities and substantive examination of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit certificate requirement (applications filed before Dec 31, 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application for which a micro-organism is to be deposited includes the fact of deposit and the deposit number, but not a copy of the deposit certificate, an examiner shall consider that the micro-organism is not deposited and conduct examination on the application. However, where an applicant failed to attach a copy of the deposit certificate and then attach the copy of the deposit certificate after being notified of a ground for rejection from an examiner, the examiner shall accept the copy and conduct examination on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copy of certificate omitted at filing, examiner treats organism as not deposited; applicant may remedy after notification of rejection and examiner shall accept the certificate when submitted in response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of deposit number by amendment is new matter (pre-2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the original specification of an application where a micro-organism is to be deposited did not state the deposit number and then the number is disclosed through amendment, it shall be deemed to be the addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amending in a deposit number that was not originally present = prohibited addition of new matter (pre-2015 rule described).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name change after reclassification: evidential document rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a micro-organism is deposited and the deposit certificate is attached before filing and relevant facts such as deposit numbers in the specification, but the patent classification of the deposited micro-organism is adjusted and then its name is changed, if a copy of the evidential document issued by a depository institution is submitted, it shall not be deemed to be the addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If classification/name changes due to depository adjustment, submitting the depository's evidential document avoids new-matter objection; but if newly-adjusted classification includes scientific characteristics not disclosed originally, stating those characteristics is new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit timing and completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposit of micro-organisms shall be completed by the time of filing the application. The time of the deposit of micro-organisms shall be deemed to be the date when the applicant deposits the concerned micro-organisms to a depository institution and then the depository institution receives the micro-organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits are meant to supplement description so a person skilled in the art can practice the invention; failure to have deposit completed by filing (or to submit certificate) may mean the deposit is treated as never made for the filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit deposit certificate after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant filed an application by only disclosing the deposit number on the specification and failed to submit the deposit certificate through amendment even after filing the application, it shall be deemed that the deposit has never been made on the date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely stating a deposit number in the spec without providing the certificate (and failing to supply it later) results in treating the deposit as not made at the claimed date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination for microorganism deposits (post-Jan 1, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proving documents are attached to an application without indicating an intention of filing the application as filing an application or vice versa, this case is considered to contravene the relevant rule so that amendments shall be proposed under Article 46 of the Patent Act of Korea. Where the deficiency is not remedied, a proceeding relevant to deposit (of microorganism) shall be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities check includes verifying that proving documents correctly indicate the intention and that deposits were made before filing; deficiencies must be communicated and amended under Article 46 or the deposit proceeding can be invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities check: deposit must precede filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent applicant submits a patent application stating the intention of the invention involving a microorganism and the proving documents, formalities check should be performed whether microorganism stated in the proving documents is deposited before filing a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must confirm the deposit date precedes filing; if not, require remedy or risk invalidation of deposit proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and remedy of deposit deficiencies (post-2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where microorganism is not deposited before filing or the name of the depositary authority, the depositary number and the depositary date are incorrectly stated in the patent application and the proving documents, the deficiencies shall be communicated to the patent applicant and be proposed to remedy. Where the deficiencies are not remedied in response to the amendment proposal within a time limit specified, a proceeding related to the deposit of micro-organisms can be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies such as non-deposit or incorrect deposit data must be notified; failure to remedy in time can invalidate the deposit proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination when deposit-related deficiencies absent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are no deficiencies identified in the documents submitted by a patent applicant, substantive examination shall be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formal proving documents are in order, proceed to substantive patentability examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositary number indication formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of depositary number by depositary authority shall be as follows: (examples: KCTC No.P, KCCM No.P, KCTC No.BP, KCCM No.P, KCLRF BP No., etc. — domestic/int'l/general deposit formats shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed authority-specific format when indicating depositary numbers in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure for microorganism inventions (enablement/support)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a person skilled in the art to practice an invention of microorganism, either (①) where a person skilled in the art can easily get microorganism, the description should, in detail, establish the process of obtaining the final product microorganism from starting material, together with the process of getting microorganism; or (②) where a person skilled in the art cannot easily get microorganism and it is difficult to establish the process in the description, the embodiment can be supported by depositing the final product microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deposit not made, the embodiment can still be supported by specifying the process sufficiently in the description to enable practice; deposit is a supplement when direct description is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing inclusion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to file a patent application including nucleic acid sequence or amino acid sequence shall include the sequence list written according to the method decided by the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office in the specification and attach the electronic file containing the sequence list drawn in the method set by the Commissioner to the patent application. However, where the sequence list drawn according to the method is disclosed in the specification in the electronic form, the electronic file of sequence list does not need to be attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings must follow KIPO's prescribed format and an electronic file must be attached unless the spec itself includes the sequence in the required electronic form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence list method and directive
rubrics_metrics.description: Details regarding the method of writing sequence list and electronic file of sequence list shall be based on the guideline for writing nucleic acid sequence or amino acid sequence (KIPO Directive No. 2013-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow KIPO Directive No.2013-1 for formatting and electronic submission specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification controls if discrepancy between spec and electronic sequence list
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the sequence list disclosed in the specification and the sequence list contained in the electronic file are different, the examiner shall examine the application based on the sequence list disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflict exists, the sequence list in the written specification governs examination (over the attached electronic file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to sequence lists treated mutatis mutandis
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination guideline for sequence list inclusion and electronic files shall apply mutatis mutandis to amendments to the sequence list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for initial submission also apply to sequence-list amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to disclose sequence list in specification (enablement rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention disclosed in claims cannot be easily practiced because the sequence list is not disclosed in the specification, an examiner shall notify a ground for rejection under Article 42(3)(i) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omission of required sequence data in the spec that renders claims non-enabled triggers a rejection under the specified Article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic sequence file missing is formality irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the electronic file of the sequence list is not attached in the application (except where the sequence list is disclosed in the specification in the electronic form), this shall be subject to amendment because of violation of the method set by orders under the Patent Act. The examiner shall request an amendment under Article 46 and if irregularities are not addressed, invalidate the application proceeding. The image-scanned sequence list is not the electronic file and is treated as not attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image scans are unacceptable; missing electronic file = request for amendment, and possible invalidation if not remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention having industrial applicability is patentable; 'industry' is interpreted broadly to cover all useful activities and practical technologies. Under Article 29(1), inventions that are publicly known/practiced or published/made available prior to filing are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must assess whether invention can be applied in industry (broad meaning). If not industrially applicable, cite Article 29(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory invention must utilize a law of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Patent Act Article 2(1), 'Invention means the highly advanced creation of a technical idea using the laws of nature'; the invention must satisfy statutory requirements and utilize a law of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish statutory inventions from utility innovations; 'highly advanced' is a relative concept and not determinative for statutory invention in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws of nature as such are non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws of nature such as the second law of thermodynamics or the law of conservation of energy are not considered to be a statutory invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pure scientific laws or principles cannot be patented as inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere discoveries are non-statutory; isolated natural things may be statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere discovery is not deemed to be a creation. However, if things in nature are isolated artificially from their surroundings, the methods, the isolated chemical substances or microorganisms are considered to be a statutory invention. A use invention claiming a new use of a known material may be patentable if closely related and non-obvious relative to the newly found property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolation/technical treatment of natural products can create statutory inventions; new-use claims require non-obvious link to newly found property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions contrary to laws of nature are non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: Those contrary to laws of nature (e.g., perpetual motion) are not considered as a statutory invention because an invention must utilize a law of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims relying on impossible physical means should be rejected as non-statutory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter not utilizing laws of nature (abstract/mental/economic methods) is non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claimed invention uses laws other than a law of nature (e.g., economic laws, mathematical methods, logics, cartography, arbitrary arrangements, or mental activities), the claimed invention is not considered statutory. However, if technical devices or methods produce concrete, tangible useful results (e.g., increase/control performance of technical tools) they may be deemed statutory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the claimed invention as a whole: presence of technical means producing objective, repeatable effects may render otherwise-abstract subject matter statutory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal skill is non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: A personal skill acquired by personal practice cannot be shared objectively and so is not considered to be a statutory invention (examples: methods of performing musical instruments, particular throwing method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims to purely personal, non-objective skills should be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere presentation of information is non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere presentation of information where the technical feature resides solely in the content of the information and its main objective is to present the information is not considered statutory. However, if the technical feature resides in the means of presentation or the presentation per se, it might be considered statutory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish content-only information from technical presentation means (the latter can be patentable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic creations per se are non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetic creation itself (e.g., paintings, carvings as such) is not considered a statutory invention. If the aesthetic creation is achieved by technical composition or other technical means, it may be viewed as statutory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artworks are not patentable unless produced/achieved by technical means that are the subject of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer program per se non-statutory; computer-implemented inventions may be statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: A computer program is a mere list of instructions and is not considered a statutory invention. However, inventions where data processing is specifically executed using hardware, a data processing unit operating with the program, operating methods, a computer-readable medium carrying the program, and the program stored in medium (applied to applications filed on/after July 1, 2014) are considered statutory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should emphasize technical implementation/hardware interaction to be patent-eligible; mere program listings are not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes that are not achievable or reproducible are non-statutory
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention whose outcome of the claimed subject matter is not achievable and reproducible is not considered statutory, even if means to achieve the goal are described. Less than 100% reproducibility can be acceptable if it is certain that outcome is achievable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require realistic reproducibility; impossible or purely speculative claims should be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete invention (enablement/support requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory invention shall be complete: subject matters must be specified clearly and thoroughly so a person with ordinary skill can easily reproduce the invention to achieve the intended technical effect. An incomplete invention at filing cannot be amended later to correct incompleteness; deficiencies in description may be corrected by amendment if invention is otherwise complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish completeness (cannot be cured post-filing) from description defects (may be amendable). Notify rejection under Article 42(3)(i) preferentially if unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grounds for rejection for non-statutory inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application falls under non-statutory categories (laws of nature, discovery, contrary to laws of nature, not using law of nature, mere presentation of information, aesthetic creations, incomplete invention), the ground for rejection shall be notified with the ground that the invention does not involve 'inventions that have industrial applicability', citing Article 29(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for rejection should cite Article 29(1) main paragraph and specify relevant reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Patent Act and Utility Model Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Patent Act, the product (including a composition) and method can be patentable. Under the Utility Model Act, a utility model may be granted only for utility innovations that relate to the shape or construction of an article or a combination of articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Utility Model Act analysis when claims are directed to shape/construction of articles; other subject matter belongs to patent regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model 'article' characteristics: shape, construction, combination
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Shape' is external figuration (lines, surfaces); 'construction' is spatial/3D construction expressed in contour, plans, elevations; 'combination' is two or more spatially separate articles that functionally relate (e.g., bolt and nut).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether claimed subject matter is an article/quasi-article under utility model criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility innovations not relating to shape/construction are not statutory utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility innovations on a method, composition, chemical substance, a thing not fixed in shape, animal or plant variety do not fall under statutory utility innovations under the Utility Model Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such subject matter should be examined under the Patent Act rather than Utility Model Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical practice generally industrially inapplicable (human treatment/diagnostic methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for treatment of the human body by surgery or therapy and a diagnostic method practiced on the human body are considered to be industrially inapplicable inventions. Surgery or treatment practiced on humans by non-medical personnel is considered medical activity. Methods that include medical activities as indispensable parts in claims are not industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish purely medical practice claims from technical/analytical methods; exclude clinical-judgment methods from patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement/analysis methods without clinical judgment may be industrially applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes which do not call for clinical judgment (e.g., detecting a tumor marker by antigen-antibody reaction to provide diagnostic information) are recognized as industrially applicable even if related to diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims directed to data collection/analysis separated from clinical judgment may be patentable; check whether method directly influences human body consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical devices and operating methods are industrially applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: A medical device used in operations on the human body or used in medical cure and diagnosis, and medical products as such are considered industrially applicable. A method for operating a medical device or measurement with the device, when the device is newly invented, is considered industrially applicable except when the method includes mutual reactions between a human body and device constituting practical medical activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device claims and device-operation methods are patentable provided they do not constitute medical practice per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods on extracted human samples are industrially applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: A method for treating samples extracted from a human body (blood, urine, cells, tissue) or discharged (urine, excrement, placenta, hair, nail) and methods for gathering data by analyzing such samples are considered industrially applicable on the assumption that they are composed of separate steps separable from medical practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should frame sample-handling and analysis steps as separable laboratory techniques rather than clinical treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal-limited methods may be industrially applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a method could be used for human treatment, the method is considered industrially applicable if it is limited to be practiced on animal bodies excluded from humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting claim scope to non-human animals can render otherwise-medical methods patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions only for personal, academic, or experimental use are industrially inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention only for personal use, academic or experimental purposes is regarded as industrially inapplicable. Inventions concerning marketable or tradable subject matter are considered industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate commercial/industrial applicability; purely private or research-only uses may be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions clearly impossible to practice are industrially inapplicable
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention which cannot be implemented or practiced is not considered industrially applicable even if it works in theory. However, if it is possible to be used in industry in the future, it may be considered industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess practicability realistically; future practical applicability can suffice but speculative impossibilities are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty exclusions under Article 29(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention publicly known or practiced, or published in a publication, or made available to the public via telecommunications prior to filing of a patent application is not novel and thus not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct prior-art assessment across global public disclosures up to the exact filing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and timing of 'publicly known' and 'publicly practiced'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Publicly known' means contents known to an unspecified person without obligation of secrecy prior to filing; 'publicly practiced' means practiced under conditions where contents are publicly known or can potentially be publicly known. The time 'prior to filing' refers to the exact point in time of filing (hour and minute) converted to Korean time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise filing time for novelty cut-off; consider examples where observing manufacturing processes or exposure to unspecified persons makes practice public.
